new_note: *Then saith Yahusha (Jesus) unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God), and him only shalt thou serve.* (Matthew 4:10). *And of the eternal judgments and torments of Gehenna, and of the prince of this world, and of his angels, and his authorities and his powers.* (Ascension of Isaiah 1:3). The Ascension of Isaiah opens its message by promising to speak of the judgment waiting for the prince of this world, and for the angels, authorities and powers who stand with him. In the wilderness the devil had just shown Yahusha (Jesus) the kingdoms of the world, and Yahusha (Jesus) does not bargain with him. He answers out of what is written, that Yahuah (God) alone is to be worshipped, and sends the adversary away. The ruler of this age is a ruler whose end is already appointed, and the Son dismisses him with a word of Torah.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 1:3 — *the prince of this world, and of his angels, and his authorities and his powers.* The ruler of this age and his powers have a judgment appointed, and Yahusha (Jesus) sends him away in the wilderness.
flag: Old note quoted words that belong to Ascension of Isaiah 3:13 (Beliar's wrath against Isaiah for the vision), not 1:3. I did not move the card, since 3:13 is not the neighbouring verse; I wrote to what 1:3 actually says (the prince of this world and his powers under judgment) and kept the Matthew 4:10 link. If you want the Beliar-wrath point, the card belongs on 3:13.

new_note: *Again, the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;* (Matthew 4:8). *After it is consummated, Beliar the great ruler, the king of this world, will descend, who hath ruled it since it came into being; yea, he will descent from his firmament in the likeness of a man, a lawless king, the slayer of his mother: who himself (even) this king.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:2). The Ascension of Isaiah says that Beliar is the king of this world and has ruled it since it came into being. When the devil takes Yahusha (Jesus) up the mountain and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, he is showing what he holds for the present age, so the offer that follows was no empty boast. But the same passage speaks of the completion of the world, and a rule that was given for a season is a rule with an end.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 4:2 — *Beliar the great ruler, the king of this world, will descend, who hath ruled it since it came into being.* The Ascension of Isaiah names the one who has ruled this world from the beginning, and the devil offers Yahusha (Jesus) what he holds.
flag: Live text of 4:2 carries a misprint, 'he will descent' (for 'descend'); quoted exactly as it stands. Old note quoted a different wording of the verse than the live text and used the phrases 'the Hebrew library' and 'Watcher-rebellion administration', which I dropped.

new_note: *Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.* (Matthew 10:4). *Will persecute the plant which the Twelve Apostles of the Beloved have planted. Of the Twelve one will be delivered into his hands.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:3). Before the Twelve are ever named, the Ascension of Isaiah says that the ruler of this world will persecute what they plant and that one of the Twelve will fall into his hands. Matthew's list of the apostles closes on exactly that note, with the last name carrying the word betrayed. Nothing in the account takes the Beloved by surprise. The persecution of the plant and the loss of one from the inner circle were spoken of ahead of time, and Matthew's commissioning of the Twelve goes on to warn them of what is coming.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 4:3 — *Of the Twelve one will be delivered into his hands.* The persecution of the plant and the loss of one of the Twelve were told in advance, and Matthew's list ends on the one who betrayed.
flag: Old note's phrase list (wisdom-stream, architecture elements) removed. 4:3 begins mid-sentence in the live text ('Will persecute...'); its subject is the ruler of 4:2.

new_note: *And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.* (Matthew 4:9). *And they will sacrifice to him and they will serve him saying: "This is Elohim (God) and beside him there is no other." And they greater number of those who shall have been associated together in order to receive the Beloved, he will turn aside after him.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:8–9). Satan asks Yahusha (Jesus) for worship, and Yahusha (Jesus) refuses. The Ascension of Isaiah shows what the same ruler gets from the world in the days of the end: sacrifice and service, and the cry that there is no other god beside him, and then the greater number of those gathered to receive the Beloved turned aside after him. It is the same grab for worship, once refused by the Son in the wilderness, and then carried out on the many who do not hold fast.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 4:9 — *those who shall have been associated together in order to receive the Beloved, he will turn aside after him.* The ruler who asked the Son for worship turns aside the greater number of those gathered to receive the Beloved.
flag: Live text of 4:9 has a misprint, 'And they greater number' (for 'the'); quoted exactly. I quoted 4:8 with it because the worship the verse is about is in 4:8. Old note quoted wording from earlier in chapter 4 (the ruler speaking as the Beloved and saying he is Elohim), not 4:9; I kept its point (the worship grab) and anchored it on what 4:8 to 4:9 says.

new_note: *And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.* (Matthew 27:35). *And the god of that world will stretch forth his hand against the Son, and they will crucify Him on a tree, and will slay Him not knowing who He is.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:14). The Ascension of Isaiah puts the weight where it belongs. The one who stretches out his hand against the Son is the god of that world, the adversary behind the deed, and those who carry it out do so not knowing who He is. Matthew then tells it as it happened, that they crucified him and divided his garments, in keeping with what the prophet had said. The tree is the place of the curse that falls on a people for breaking the covenant, and the Son took that curse on himself, so that the scattered might come home to the Torah, not away from it.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 9:14 — *will stretch forth his hand against the Son, and they will crucify Him on a tree.* The deed is traced to the god of that world, and those who did it did not know who He was.
flag: Old note's 'FRAMEWORK-MAJOR', S-number and Red Line references removed. Keeps the old note's point that the curse borne is the exile judgment and not the Torah; no other theology added.

new_note: *And thus His descent, as you will see, will be hidden even from the heavens, so that it will not be known who He is.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:15). *For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him.* (Isaiah 53:2). The Ascension of Isaiah says the Son's coming down will be hidden even from the heavens, so that none will know who He is. Isaiah had already spoken of this long before, of one who grows up like a tender plant, with no form or comeliness to draw the eye. The powers of heaven did not recognize him as he passed through, and the people on earth did not see anything in him to desire.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 9:15 — *His descent, as you will see, will be hidden even from the heavens.* The descent hidden from the heavens matches Isaiah's tender plant with no form or comeliness.

new_note: *Yahusha (Jesus), when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.* (Matthew 27:50). *And when He hath plundered the angel of death, He will ascend on the third day, and he will remain in that world five hundred and forty-five days.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:16). Matthew tells that Yahusha (Jesus) cried out and yielded up the ghost, and the verb is his own: he gave himself up. The Ascension of Isaiah says what that death was for. He goes down and plunders the angel of death, and on the third day he ascends. The death at the cross is the doorway of the descent, and the descent ends in the rising.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 9:16 — *when He hath plundered the angel of death, He will ascend on the third day.* The Son who yielded up the ghost at the cross plunders the angel of death and rises on the third day.

new_note: *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52). *And then many of the righteous will ascend with Him, whose spirits do not receive their garments till Yahuah (Lord) Messiah (Christ) ascend and they ascend with Him.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:17). Matthew says the graves were opened and many bodies of the saints which slept arose. The Ascension of Isaiah says why the righteous waited as they did: their spirits do not receive their garments until the Messiah ascends, and then many of them ascend with him. Those who walked the covenant faithfully and slept are the first to be brought out when the way is opened, and the opened graves at the cross are a foretaste of the larger rising still to come.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 9:17 — *many of the righteous will ascend with Him, whose spirits do not receive their garments.* The righteous who sleep wait for the Messiah's ascension, and Matthew shows the first of them rising.

new_note: *And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed.* (Matthew 27:60). *And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:19). Matthew closes the day with the body laid in a new tomb cut in the rock and a great stone rolled to the door. The Ascension of Isaiah tells where the Beloved was while the body lay there: after they crucified Him, He descended to the angel of Sheol. The same verse says the adversary envied him and stirred up the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against him, not knowing who He was. The charge lies with the adversary who envied and stirred, and a people who did not know who they were handing over are the lost sheep, not enemies.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:19 — *they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* While the body lay in the sealed tomb, the Beloved went down to the angel of Sheol.
flag: Old note's reading of the Isaiah 53:9 tomb (rich man's grave) and its Red Line reference dropped from the text; kept its point that the verse is not a charge against the Yahudim (Jews) as a people.

new_note: *Now when they were going, behold, some of the watch came into the city, and shewed unto the chief priests all the things that were done.* (Matthew 28:11). *And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:19). Matthew tells that some of the watch came into the city and showed the chief priests all that had been done, and the verses that follow tell of money given to the soldiers to carry a false story. The Ascension of Isaiah gives the order of it: the adversary envied him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against him, not knowing who He was. The line runs from the adversary through those who held the seat of leadership, and the many who were roused did not know, and are deceived sheep. It is a system that lied, and no verse here makes a whole people the enemy.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:19 — *the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was.* The adversary roused the people not knowing who He was, and Matthew shows the leadership answering the truth with a cover story.
flag: Same extra verse as card 4889 (11:19); this card carries the system-not-people point, 4889 the burial and descent. Old note's internal references removed.

new_note: *And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.* (Matthew 27:35). *In Jerusalem indeed I saw Him being crucified on a tree:* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:20). Matthew tells of the crucifixion in a few plain lines and says it came to pass according to what was spoken by the prophet. The Ascension of Isaiah has Isaiah himself seeing it first, and naming the place: in Jerusalem, on a tree. What Matthew sets down as history, the prophet was shown beforehand.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:20 — *In Jerusalem indeed I saw Him being crucified on a tree.* Isaiah is shown the crucifixion ahead of time, in Jerusalem, on a tree.

new_note: *He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6). *And likewise after the third day rise again and remain days.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:21). At the empty tomb the angel says that he is not here, for he is risen, as he said. The Ascension of Isaiah has Isaiah told the same in vision, that He will rise after the third day and remain days. The rising was not an afterthought, it was said before by Yahusha (Jesus) himself and seen before by the prophet, and the days he remained with his own after rising are the days the vision speaks of.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:21 — *after the third day rise again and remain days.* Isaiah is shown the rising after the third day and the days He remained, which the angel at the tomb announces as fulfilled.
flag: Old note named the forty days of Acts 1:3; I kept only a general sentence about the days He remained, since the live verse says only 'remain days'.

new_note: *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). *And the angel who conducted me said: "Understand, Isaiah": and I saw when He sent out the Twelve Apostles and ascended.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:22). Isaiah sees Him send out the Twelve Apostles and then ascend, and Matthew has the sending in his own words: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations. Twelve are sent because the twelve tribes are the ones being sought, and the nations are where the scattered of those tribes now live. We do not know the sheep by sight, so the word goes out broadly, and the sheep hear his voice.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:22 — *I saw when He sent out the Twelve Apostles and ascended.* The sending of the Twelve and the ascension are seen together, as Matthew's last words to the Twelve are spoken.
flag: Old note's Great Commission reading (the Twelve match the twelve tribes; the scattered among the nations) kept in plain prose; Matthew 19:28 and Revelation 21:14, which it cited, are not quoted here.

new_note: *Both worshipped Him and praised Him and said: "How did our Lord escape us whilst descending, and we perceived not?"* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:26). *Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.* (Revelation 5:12). In the Ascension of Isaiah, the powers of the heavens worship the Beloved as he passes through and ask how He went by them unseen, and at each heaven the same praise is given again. John's vision of the throne room has the same voice going up, loud and many: Worthy is the Lamb that was slain. The praise the angels give in Isaiah's vision is the praise of Revelation, given to the one who was slain.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:26 — *How did our Lord escape us whilst descending, and we perceived not?.* The heavens worship the Beloved who passed through unseen, as they cry Worthy is the Lamb in Revelation.

new_note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18). *And I saw how He ascended into the seventh heaven, and all the righteous and all the angels praised Him. And then I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory I told you that I could not behold.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:32). The Ascension of Isaiah says He sat down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory the prophet could not behold. The Great Glory is the Father, the formless one, and the Son who took form sits at his right hand. When Yahusha (Jesus) says in Matthew that all power is given unto him in heaven and in earth, the word given tells the same story: the Son receives the power from the Father who gives it, and takes his seat beside him.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:32 — *I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory.* The Son sits at the right hand of the Great Glory, the Father, and Matthew has him say that all power is given unto him.
flag: Kept the Father/Son point: the Great Glory is the Father (formless), the Son receives the power as given. No doctrine asserted beyond that.

new_note: *And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;* (Matthew 27:51). *And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.* (2 Baruch 6:7). The veil is torn from the top to the bottom, which is a tearing from above. In 2 Baruch the hand from above also acts upon the veil: the angel descends into the Holy of Holies and takes from there the veil, the ark, the mercy seat and every holy vessel, and the next verse in the book says he charges the earth to guard them until the last times so that strangers may not get possession of them. In neither is the house of Yahuah (God) simply done away with. In Baruch its holy things are kept to be restored, and in Matthew the veil is opened from above, and the way back into the holiest is the way home.
member_note: 2 Baruch 6:7 — *I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark.* The angel who descends and takes the veil in 2 Baruch is the hand from above that tears the veil in Matthew.
flag: Old note cited the Charles edition numbering (seq #3); the live book is 2 Baruch 6:7. I kept its point that the veil is opened from above and the Father's house is not abolished; I dropped the references to internal exposition. The 'him' of 6:7 is the angel who was sent (6:6) and not the Messiah.

new_note: *And it shall come to pass at that self-same time that the treasury of manna shall again descend from on high, and they will eat of it in those years, because these are they who have come to the consummation of time.* (2 Baruch 29:8). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.* (John 6:35). In the years of the Messiah, 2 Baruch says, the treasury of manna will again descend from on high, and they will eat of it. The bread that came down for the tribes in the wilderness is promised again for the end of time. Yahusha (Jesus) says of himself that he is the bread of life, and that the one who comes to him shall never hunger and the one who believes on him shall never thirst. The bread from on high that Baruch looks for is the one standing before them in John.
member_note: 2 Baruch 29:8 — *the treasury of manna shall again descend from on high.* The manna promised again from on high is the bread of life Yahusha (Jesus) names himself.
flag: Old note's phrase 'the saved feed' removed. Kept the connection; nothing added.

new_note: *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52). *But those who have been saved by their works, And to whom the law has been now a hope, And understanding an expectation, And wisdom a confidence, Shall wonders appear in their time. For they shall behold the world which is now invisible to them, And they shall behold the time which is now hidden from them:* (2 Baruch 51:7–8). Matthew says the graves were opened and many bodies of the saints which slept arose. Baruch speaks of people for whom the law was a hope, an understanding and a confidence, and says wonders will appear in their time and they will behold the world that is now invisible to them. These are people whose whole life was the Torah, and nothing here sets their works against the promise. It describes the covenant walk of those who kept the commandments, and the opened graves at the cross are the first glimpse of the seeing that is promised to them.
member_note: 2 Baruch 51:7 — *to whom the law has been now a hope, And understanding an expectation, And wisdom a confidence.* Those for whom the law was a hope are promised sight of the invisible world, and Matthew shows the sleeping saints beginning to rise.
flag: 'Saved by their works' read as the covenant walk of the Torah-keeping righteous (law as hope), not a works-against-faith statement; no merit doctrine. The old note spanned 51:7 and 51:8 and quoted a combined 'standard 51:1-8' form; I quote 51:7 and 51:8 in order. Old note's Charles seq #21 numbering is stale.

new_note: *Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;* (Matthew 9:37). *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.* (2 Baruch 70:2). Baruch looks ahead to the time when the age has ripened and the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, and the Mighty One brings bewilderment on the earth and its rulers. Yahusha (Jesus), looking at the crowds, says the harvest truly is plenteous, and the labourers are few. What Baruch placed at the end of the age, Yahusha (Jesus) says is already at hand. Both speak of a harvest of two kinds of seed, which is why the sorting matters and why labourers are wanted.
member_note: 2 Baruch 70:2 — *the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come.* The harvest of the age, evil and good seeds together, is the harvest Yahusha (Jesus) says is already plenteous.
flag: Old note cited 2 Baruch 35:1 (stale numbering); the quoted words are in the live 2 Baruch 70:2, and the card sits on 70:2. The 'good and evil seeds' read as the two kinds sown together until harvest; no further claim made.
